Name: Edwin F. Bryant
Specialism: Yoga Sūtras, Hindu philosophy, Krishna traditions
Notable Works: The Yoga Sūtras of Patañjali (trans.); Krishna: A Sourcebook
Credibility Notes: PhD Indology (Columbia); respected in both academic and practitioner yoga communities — unusually well-bridged voice.

Name: Barbara Stoler Miller
Specialism: Sanskrit literature, Yoga Sūtras, Bhagavad Gītā
Notable Works: Yoga: Discipline of Freedom; The Bhagavad-Gita (trans.)
Credibility Notes: One of the leading Sanskrit translators of her generation; her Gītā is a recognised classic.

Name: James Mallinson
Specialism: Haṭha yoga, Sanskrit manuscripts, ascetic traditions
Notable Works: Roots of Yoga; Haṭha Yoga Project critical editions
Credibility Notes: Leading authority on haṭha yoga's textual history; also an initiated mahant in the Rāmānandī order — scholar-practitioner.

Name: Mark Singleton
Credibility Notes: His Yoga Body thesis reshaped the field and remains contested — know both the argument and the Hindu critiques of it.

Name: Andrea R. Jain
Specialism: Modern yoga, religion and consumer culture
Credibility Notes: Peer-reviewed scholar of yoga's commercialisation; critical of both commodification and nationalist origin claims.

Name: Elizabeth De Michelis
Credibility Notes: Founded modern yoga studies as a subfield; her fourfold typology of Modern Yoga is standard reference.

Name: Pancham Sinh
Credibility Notes: Public-domain colonial-era translator; serviceable free text but terminology is dated — check against modern scholarship.

Name: SOAS Hatha Yoga Project
Specialism: History of physical yoga: philology and ethnography
Notable Works: Critical editions and translations of ten haṭha yoga texts
Credibility Notes: Major peer-reviewed research project (2015–20); outputs freely available.

Name: The British Museum
Specialism: South Asian art and material religion
Credibility Notes: World-class curation (South Asia curator Imma Ramos); note ongoing debates about colonial-era collections.

Name: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art
Credibility Notes: First major museum treatment of yoga's visual history; reliable public scholarship.

Name: Wellcome Collection
Notable Works: Ayurvedic Man: Encounters with Indian Medicine (exhibition)
Credibility Notes: Strong free online resources on Indian medical traditions from a history-of-medicine angle.

Name: B.K.S. Iyengar
Institution / Affiliation: Ramamani Iyengar Memorial Yoga Institute, Pune (d. 2014)
Notable Works: Light on Yoga; Light on Prāṇāyāma
Credibility Notes: The most influential yoga teacher of the 20th century; practitioner authority, not academic scholarship.

Name: T.K.V. Desikachar
Credibility Notes: Son and student of Krishnamacharya; transmits the lineage behind much of modern yoga from inside.

Name: Christopher D. Wallis
Credibility Notes: Scholar-practitioner: trained academically but writes devotionally for practitioners; not peer-reviewed.

Name: Bihar School of Yoga
Notable Works: Yoga Magazine; Asana Pranayama Mudra Bandha
Credibility Notes: Major living Indian yoga institution; single-lineage perspective with decades of free archives.

Name: Hindu American Foundation
Notable Works: Hindu Roots of Yoga / Take Back Yoga campaign
Credibility Notes: Advocacy organisation, not scholarship — politically engaged and contested, but a key voice in the yoga-ownership debate.

Name: Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies
Notable Works: OCHS lecture podcast archive; OCHS Online courses
Credibility Notes: Your own institution — in-house lectures and courses; academically grounded with practitioner sensitivity.

Name: TED-Ed
Credibility Notes: High production educational shorts; reliable for orientation, always check the named author of each lesson.

Name: Revision World
Credibility Notes: Exam-focused summaries; useful scaffolding, not a citable source.
